take_homes: Take access away after adding context: every door I don't open is a risk I don't have to name or retest.
The saved security check is one skill with two lenses, policy and agent risk. I rerun it and share it with my team.
A document the agent reads can steer it, so checking means finding 'I can't tell' rows and taking those to the owner.

monday.move: Run the saved agent-audit skill against the pricing-pilot brief setup, pick the top risk, and close one door, such as write access or an unneeded mailbox.
monday.who: Me, then one teammate who installs the skill
monday.when: Monday morning before the pricing working group
monday.stop_condition: One risk has a mitigation and a written residual, and the 'I can't tell' rows are listed for legal
monday.blocker: Our shared place for context files doesn't exist, so the teammate gets a copy of the skill, not a shared one.

misconception.why: The saved skill, not a prompt, carries the judgment into the next session and to a teammate, so prompt quality is not what makes this useful. I still half-think better prompts matter.

one_line: Good hour on closing doors and a check my team can rerun, but cut the 'rapidly evolving area' paragraphs, they appear nine times.
